Rashi on Arakhin 20a:11:1.hebrew: על בהמה - אם אמר: דמי בהמתי עלי, הנדר חל. אבל ערך אינו אלא באדם:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:11:1.english: On a domesticated animal - If one said, "The value of my animal is incumbent upon me," [the vow takes effect]. But a valuation applies only to a person:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:11:2.hebrew: ואינן נידונין בהשג יד - שאם אמר: ״דמי עלי״, ואין ידו משגת, יתן הכל לכשיוכל:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:11:2.english: And they are not assessed based on affordability - For if one said, "My value is incumbent upon me," and he cannot afford it, he must give all of it when he is able:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:13:1.hebrew: ש"מ מלוה על פה כו' - ופלוגתא היא בכמה דוכתי:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:13:1.english: One can conclude [that] a loan by oral agreement, etc. - And this is a matter of dispute in several places:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:14:1.hebrew: ש"מ מלוה הכתובה כו' - ופלוגתא היא במס' בכורות בפ' יש בכור לנחלה (דף מט:):
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:14:1.english: [One can] conclude [that] a loan that is written [in the Torah] etc. - And this is a matter of dispute in tractate Bekhorot, in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor LeNachalah (page 49b):

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:14:2.hebrew: כשעמד בדין - וחייבוהו בית דין קודם מותו, דה"ל כמלוה בשטר:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:14:2.english: Where he stood in judgment - and [the court] obligated him before his death, so that it is considered like a loan [written] in a document:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:15:1.hebrew: אמאי לא יתנו יורשין - דמי עלי, הרי אמדוהו ב"ד:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:15:1.english: Why shouldn't the heirs give - [in the case of "the valuation [dmei] of me is incumbent upon me"]? Surely the court has [already] assessed him:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:15:2.hebrew: מחסרא אומדנא - שחייבוהו לשלם, ולא הספיקו לאומדו עד שמת:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:15:2.english: The assessment is lacking - [This refers to a case] where [the court] obligated him to pay, but they did not manage to assess him before he died:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:17:1.hebrew: לא אמר כלום לרבנן - דאמרי בפ"ק (לעיל ערכין ה.): אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:17:1.english: "He has not said anything" according to the Rabbis - for they say in the first chapter (above, Arakhin 5a) that a person [may] utter his words for naught:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:17:2.hebrew: נותן דמיו - ואוקימנא בפ"ק דערכין דאליבא דר"מ אמרה:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:17:2.english: He gives its value - And we established in the first chapter [of Arakhin] that [the mishna] was stated in accordance with Rabbi Meir:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:19:1.hebrew: אבל דמי לא קאמר - והלכך לא ליתיב דמי, ורב גידל קמ"ל:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:19:1.english: But he did not say "assessments" - and therefore he should not give [the] assessment [value]; [Rav Giddel] teaches us [otherwise]:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:1:1.hebrew: בחד זימנא אמדינן ליה - והוא נותן פי שנים בדמים של אותה הערכה יתן:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:1:1.english: We assess him once - he gives twice [the amount] in value [of that single assessment]:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:25:1.english: A vow with regard to your valuation - Vows [of assessment] were juxtaposed to valuations:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:27:1.hebrew: ל"ש כולו ול"ש חציו - ואשמועינן רבי מאיר בחציו, וכ"ש בכולו: דאע"ג דלאו אורחא לאינדובי חצי דמי כלי, אפ"ה יהיב, וכ"ש כולו:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:27:1.english: There is no difference [whether he vowed] the whole of it or half of it - And [Rabbi Meir] teaches us [this] with regard to half, and certainly with regard to the whole: even though it is not customary to pledge half the value of a vessel, nevertheless he gives [the assessment], and certainly [if he pledged] the whole of it:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:3:1.hebrew: אמדוהו מאליו - בלא שום צורך, אלא לשום דברים בעלמא, ועשרה היו שם, מהו האם נחשב כאומדן:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:3:1.english: They assessed him on its own - without any need, but merely for the sake of [idle] talk, and ten [judges] were there; what is [the law]?

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:4:1.hebrew: פשוט מהא - מתני' דלהלן, חדא מהני בעיות:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:4:1.english: Resolve from this - [from the] mishna [below], [resolve] one of these dilemmas:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:4:2.hebrew: שאין דמים למתים - ומעיקרא לא ידעינן כמה שוה:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:4:2.english: For there is no valuation for the dead - And originally [at the time of the vow] we did not know how much he was worth:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:5:1.hebrew: הא אמיד וקאי - דהא אין לך אדם שאינו שוה ד' זוזי:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:5:1.english: Isn't he [already] standing assessed - For there is no person who is not worth four zuz:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:6:1.hebrew: לא נחית לאומדנא - שלא נאמד מעולם, אלא השתא הוא דאמדינן, ואנן אומדנא בעינן:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:6:1.english: He has not entered into an assessment - [meaning] that he was never assessed; rather, it is only now that we are assessing [him], whereas we require [that there be] an [actual prior] assessment:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:7:1.hebrew: ערכי עלי - דבר קצוב הוא, הלכך יתנו היורשין:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:7:1.english: My valuation is incumbent upon me - It is a fixed amount; therefore the heirs must give [it]:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:7:2.hebrew: שאין דמים למתים - והא דתניא בב"ק (דף כז.) "ונתן פדיון נפשו" שהוא דמי ניזק, התם הוא טעמא משום דמשעתא דאזיק רמי עליה לשלומי כשעת ההיזק, וההיא שעתא דאזקיה חי הוא. אבל האומר "דמי עלי", שאינו נודר אלא מה שישומוהו ב"ד, והרי לא בא לידי כך, שהרי מת, לא יתנו היורשין:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:7:2.english: For there is no monetary value for the dead - But as for what was taught in [tractate] Bava Kamma (27a), "and he shall give the redemption of his life" [meaning] the value of the injured party — there the reason is that from the moment he caused the injury, it was incumbent upon him to pay according to the value at the time of the injury, and at that moment when he injured him, [the victim] was alive. But [one who says,] "my assessment is incumbent upon me," vows only what the court would assess him [to be worth], and this has not come about, since he died — his heirs do not have to give:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:8:1.hebrew: נותן ערך כולו - שהרי "בערכך נפשות" כתיב:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:8:1.english: He gives the valuation of his entire [self] - [This is] because it is written, "according to your valuation of persons" (Leviticus 27:2):

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:9:1.hebrew: ערך חציי עלי - הוי כערך ראשי וערך כבידי, דהוי דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:9:1.english: "The valuation of half of me is incumbent upon me" - This is like [saying] "the valuation of my head" or "the valuation of my liver," since it is an item upon which the soul is dependent:

Rashi on Arakhin 20a:9:2.hebrew: דמי חציי עלי נותן דמי כולו - דהא תניא בפרק השג יד (לעיל ערכין יח.): הקשתה דמים לערכין לידון בכבודו:
Rashi on Arakhin 20a:9:2.english: [If one says:] The assessment of half of me is incumbent upon me, he gives the assessment of his entire [self] - For it was taught in the chapter [entitled] Hasag Yad (above, Arakhin 18a): [Scripture] compared assessments to valuations, [so that the person] is assessed according to his own worth:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:11:1.hebrew: ת"ר חומר בנדרים מבערכין כו' - תימה, אמאי לא פריך אמתני' דקתני "זה חומר בנדרים מבערכין", זה חומר ותו לא? והא איכא הני דברייתא! דכה"ג פריך בב"מ פרק הזהב (בבא מציעא דף נז:) גבי הא דאמר "זה חומר בהקדש מבהדיוט", ופריך "זה חומר ותו לא? האיכא טובא"; לפרוך הכא הכי! וי"ל דהתם ליכא חידוש למצוא חומרא בהקדש מבהדיוט, דמדין הוא דיש לנו להחמיר טפי בהקדש מבהדיוט, ומש"ה קא מתמה עליה הש"ס "זה חומר ותו לא? והא איכא טובא". אבל הכא דאיכא רבותא דמחמיר טפי בנדרים מבערכין, מש"ה לא שייך למיפרך עליה "זה חומר ותו לא", דתנא ושייר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:11:1.english: The Sages taught: A stringency regarding vows over valuations, etc. - It is surprising: why does [the Gemara] not challenge the Mishnah, which teaches, "This is a stringency of vows over valuations" — [challenging:] is this the only stringency? But there are these [others] of the baraita! For in a similar case [the Gemara] challenges in Bava Metzia, in the chapter [entitled] Hazahav (Bava Metzia 57b), regarding that which it says, "This is a stringency of consecrated property over ordinary property," and it challenges, "Is this the only stringency? There are many!" [So] let it challenge here likewise! And one can answer that there, there is no novelty in finding a stringency of consecrated property over ordinary property, for it is logical that we should be more stringent with consecrated property than with ordinary property; and therefore the Gemara expresses surprise there: "Is this the only stringency? There are many!" But here, where there is a novelty in that it is more stringent with vows than with valuations, therefore it is not appropriate to challenge it with "Is this the only stringency?", since the Tanna taught [some] and left [others] out:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:11:2.hebrew: ואין נידונין בהשג יד כערכין - וקשה, שהרי הקשנו לעיל (ערכין ד' יח.): "דמים לערכין, מרגלית לקלים, ואין היקש למחצה"; ואיכא למימר דאיכא חד מיעוטא, דכתיב "יעריכנו הכהן" גבי ערכין, דמשמע ליה ולא לאחר, וגבי ערכין נידון בהשג יד, כאשר יעריכנו הכהן, ולא גבי נדרים:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:11:2.english: And they are not assessed based on affordability, as [they are] with valuations - And this is difficult, for we already raised the difficulty above (Arakhin 18a): "[Should one derive the law of] vows of assessment from valuations? [That is like comparing] a pearl to light [items], and there is no half-analogy." But one can say that there is one exclusion, as it is written "the priest shall assess him" regarding valuations, which implies [that it applies] to him and not to another; and regarding valuations, one is assessed based on affordability, "according to what the priest shall assess him," but not regarding vows of assessment:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:26:1.hebrew: לאתויי מן הארכובה ולמעלה - וא"ת, אמאי נקט מן הארכובה ולמעלה טפי מכל שאר י"ח טריפות? וי"ל, דאיכא רבותא בהאי טפי, לאפוקי דר"ש דאמר (חולין דף מב:) יכולה היא ליכוות ולחיות:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:26:1.english: To include [one who vowed the assessment of a limb] from the knee and above - If you ask: Why did [the Gemara] choose [the case of] from the knee and above, more than all the other eighteen [categories of] *terefot* [fatal defects]? And one can answer: There is a greater novelty in this [case] than in the others, to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Shimon, who said (Chullin 42b) that it [the leg] can be cauterized and live:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:3:1.hebrew: אמדוהו מאליו מהו מי אמרי' כו' - הא בעיא לא אתיא ב"ואם תמצא לומר" כמו ההיא דלעיל, ולבדה היה יכול לשאלה, אלא שרוצה לערבה עם שאר הבעיות:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:3:1.english: If they assessed him on his own, what is the halakha? Do we say, etc. - This question does not come as an "and if you will say" [question], like that one above; [the Gemara] could have asked it by itself, but it wishes to combine it with the other questions:

Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:7:1.hebrew: דמי עלי ומת לא יתנו יורשים לפי שאין דמים וכו' - והא דתניא בב"ק (דף כז. ושם): "ונתן פדיון נפשו" – דמי ניזק, פי' ששמין אותו לאחר מיתה כמה היה שוה מחיים, גזירת הכתוב היא. אבל הכא אינו נודר אלא דמים שישומוהו בב"ד, והוא לא בא לידי שומא, שהרי הוא מת, לא יתנו יורשין את דמיו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 20a:7:1.english: "My assessment is upon me," and he died, his heirs do not give, because there is no [monetary] value etc. - As for that which was taught in Bava Kamma (27a, and there): "And he shall give the redemption of his life" — [this means] the value of the one injured; meaning, that they assess him after death, [determining] how much he was worth when alive; this is a decree of the verse. But here, he vowed only an assessed value that the court would assess for him, and he did not come to assessment, since he died; [therefore] the heirs do not give his value:
